expectation: CD3E is a T-cell membrane marker: rings on a subset of small round lymphocytes, scattered as single cells in the lamina propria and intraepithelial, and clustered in lymphoid aggregates. Epithelium, stroma and other cell types should be negative.
observed: A: faint yellow tissue-wide haze with bright edge lines and a few bright specks. B/C: distinct bright membrane rings on small round cells, intraepithelial and in the lamina propria, on a hazy background. D: ring-stained cluster. E: dense bright CD3E cells in a CD4-rich aggregate, with partial CD4 overlap.
why: Discrete membrane-ringed lymphocytes sit in lamina propria, epithelium and aggregates, and overlap CD4+ cells in a dense field, despite background haze.
notes: B, C and D show crisp membrane rings on a subset of small round cells, in the lamina propria and between epithelial cells. In E, CD3E cells overlap CD4+ cells, with CD3E-only cells that fit CD8 T cells. Background haze and edge glow are present but do not carry the call.
